headline: Deep learning automates microscopy and histology image analysis with less labelled data
label: Deep Learning Bioimage Analysis Tools
summary: Recent preprints and a published toolbox benchmark deep learning on histology, MRI, OCT, and CT segmentation under cross-cohort and cross-species shift.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning applied to biomedical images, with attention to generalization and reduced reliance on manual annotation. Several items target robustness under distribution shift: CS-ARM-BN uses negative control samples to stabilize batch-normalization statistics across sources, and PanGuide3D conditions pancreatic tumor CT segmentation on a probabilistic pancreas map to hold up across cohorts. Annotation burden is addressed through weak supervision, with cell-level spatial transcriptomics generating image-label pairs for histopathology nuclei, and CHRep predicting spatial gene expression from H&E histology. FiloAnalyzer contributes an open-source GUI for batch filopodia segmentation. Other items are less uniform: the rat OCT benchmark found a CNN Xception baseline outperforming the transferred RETFound model, and the RE-CONFIRM work operates on dynamic functional connectivity rather than images. The thread is methodological rather than biological.
